sentences.text: Shri Rishiraj Trivedi - advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Kshitij Vyas - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State
ORDER Heard and perused the record.

This is first bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C, 1973) for grant of bail during trial relating to Crime No.176/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Ghatia District-Ujjain for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376(A), 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC, 1860 and under section 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 18.03.2024.
2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that of abduction and commission of rape upon the prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present crime.
The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35104 2 MCRC-52073-2024 incident happened on 21.04.2024 and FIR was lodged on 25.04.2024.
Prosecutrix is aged about 17 years and 3 months at the time of the incident and the applicant is 21 years old.

Learned counsel submitted that although it is alleged that applicant kept the prosecutrix in confinement for four days and committed rape, however, he has drawn the Court's attention especially to para-16 of the cross-examination wherein prosecutrix has admitted the material Arvind Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116176048/
1 omissions and there are ample admissions on her part.

entities.text: Arvind Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 18.03.2024.
Conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application by submitting that prosecutrix is minor therefore bail should not be granted.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the rival submissions of the counsel for the parties, custody period of the applicant, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his/her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety to the satisfaction of the trial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35104 3 MCRC-52073-2024 court for securing his/her presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
8.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified Copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE sumathi Arvind Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116176048/
